# PlanWorldSimulator world generator

Describe a planning benchmark in plain language and generate a playable world from it.
See [docs/design-decisions](docs/design-decisions) for the architecture.

The generator is a fake for now: it walks through the real steps (storyline, copy
template, fill template, tests) and writes a world folder, but does no LLM work.

## Layout

| Path                  | What it is                                                  |
| --------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `src/web`             | Website (Vite, React, TypeScript, Tailwind)                 |
| `src/backend`         | API (FastAPI, SQLite via SQLAlchemy and Alembic)            |
| `src/worlds-template` | Base template every world is copied from                    |
| `src/worlds`          | Generated worlds, one folder each (contents are gitignored) |

## Run it

```sh
just up      # build, start in the background, wait until healthy
just down    # stop (database and generated worlds are kept)
```

Open http://localhost:8480 (API docs on http://localhost:8400/docs). If another program uses
those ports, `just up` says so; set `PLANWORLDSIMULATOR_WEB_PORT` and
`PLANWORLDSIMULATOR_API_PORT` in `.env` to change them. Other commands: `just build`, `just logs [service]`,
`just ps`, `just reset` (also deletes the database volume) and `just dev` (live
reload, site on http://localhost:5173). Copy `.env.example` to `.env` to change
defaults.

## Generate real worlds

Put `GEMINI_API_KEY` in `.env`, then `just build` and `just up` as above. The API image
contains the coding agent (OpenCode), the shared world environment and Chromium, so the site
generates real worlds that you can play (about 2–5 minutes each; the first build takes a
while and the image is around 3 GB). Without a key the stack still starts and generates
fake worlds: the API log says which one it uses ("world generation: ...").

Worlds are written to `src/worlds/` on your machine. The model defaults to
`google/gemini-3.5-flash` (`PLANWORLDSIMULATOR_GENERATOR_MODEL` changes it).

Without Docker, on your machine:

```sh
just world-setup                       # once: world environment, Chromium, OpenCode check
just generate "Lemonade" "A lemonade stand ..."   # one world from the command line
just api-local                         # or: the API with the real generator and launcher
just web-local                         # the website on http://localhost:5173
```

A world has three difficulty levels, must pass its tests, and is playable from the website.
See [decision 0008](docs/design-decisions/0008-create-worlds-with-a-sandboxed-coding-agent.md).

## Develop

Needs [pixi](https://pixi.sh), [pnpm](https://pnpm.io) and [just](https://just.systems).

```sh
just install
just format
just lint
just typecheck
just test
```

Both keys are in `.env` (they're not exported in the shell, so I'll load them from there). `ffmpeg` is missing, and I need it for frame extraction and the final assembly. Here's the refined plan.

## Changes from the last version
1. **Voice:** Gradium for the voiceover, generated per segment so each line can be timed to its clip.
2. **Audio:** Omni audio is off or discarded. One consistent Gradium voice, plus music and sound effects, carries the whole video.
3. **Assembly:** Remotion does the final cut, with all the text, the diagram and the end card.
4. **Gemini product for stills:** Gemini image generation makes clean first and last frames, so the Omni clips start and end on exactly the frames I choose.

## Pipeline
```
script.md (timed lines)
  → Gradium TTS: one wav per line, measured duration
  → Gemini image: key frames (A2 start, C1 to C3 frames, where screenshots won't do)
  → Omni: 5 clips (A1, A2, C1, C2, C3), 2–3 takes each
  → ffmpeg: extract last frames to chain C1 to C2 to C3, trim to the voice length
  → Browser use: record B and E
  → Friend: record D (human and agent play)
  → Remotion: assemble clips + voice + music + captions + diagram (F) + end card (G)
```

## Voiceover script (about 280 words, one voice, confident and a little playful)

| Seg | Line | Target |
|---|---|---|
| A1 | "You think running a food truck is hard? Or playing ARC-AGI-3?" | 6s |
| A2 | "Then you've never played PlanWorldSimulator. Generate a planning world, and test your skills against the agent. Can you beat him?" | 9s |
| B | "Just describe it. A bike factory: suppliers, assembly, three shops, hidden patterns to discover." | 10s |
| C1–C3 | "No waiting for a progress bar. Your world is designed, built, tested… and shipped." | 12s |
| D | "Play it yourself, or delegate to an agent. Watch who plans better." | 8s |
| E | "Easy forgives. Medium demands planning. Hard: tight cash, and the disruptions are unpredictable." | 12s |
| F | "Under the hood, a sandboxed coding agent writes the simulator, the world view and the tests. A world ships only if it passes." | 10s |
| G | "Do you have what it takes to be a planning master?" | 4s |

I generate the voice first and measure each file. Then I set the clip lengths and the edit to match, instead of guessing.

## Open questions
1. **Segment D:** does your friend's recording show the human and the agent at the same moment, or two separate takes? Same moment suggests a split screen; separate takes suggest a cut between them.
2. **Segment E:** I'll read the difficulty config in the world to pick three real, visible differences for the voiceover and an on-screen label per level.
3. **Music:** I'd use a royalty-free track or a Gemini/Lyria-generated loop, if you have access. Otherwise I'd use a free-license track.
4. **Install:** `brew install ffmpeg` is needed. Run `! brew install ffmpeg` if you're OK with that.

## Proposed first step
I start with the cheapest, most valuable test: one Gradium line to confirm the voice and API work, then one Omni clip (C1) with a single take. I'd also read the API docs first, since I haven't verified the Gradium or Omni parameters. That checks the whole chain before we spend on all the takes.

In the end you also need to be able to concatenate all video frames please? Where should my friend place them?

Yes. The final cut is assembled in one place, so every clip needs a predictable name and a fixed spec.

## Where your friend puts the recordings
Everything lives in one folder at the repo root, which I'd create as `demo-video/`:

```
demo-video/
  inputs/
    D1_human-play.mov       ← your friend: human playing
    D2_agent-play.mov       ← your friend: agent playing
    B_generate-prompt.mov   ← browser recording of typing the prompt and clicking Generate
    E1_easy.mov  E2_medium.mov  E3_hard.mov
  generated/                ← made by me: Omni clips, key frames, voice wavs
  script.md                 ← timed voiceover lines
  timeline.json             ← ordered list of clips with start, end, and voice line
  out/final.mp4             ← the result
```

If your friend isn't working in the repo, they can send the files to you. Drop them into `demo-video/inputs/` with exactly those names, because the assembly reads them by name. Large video files shouldn't be committed. I'd add `demo-video/inputs/`, `generated/` and `out/` to `.gitignore`.

## Recording specs (for your friend)
- 1920×1080 or larger, 30 fps, screen only (audio is replaced by the voiceover).
- Browser zoom 125–150%, notifications off, clean browser profile.
- Record about 10 extra seconds at the start and end of each take, so I can trim.
- For D: the agent take should show the agent's moves clearly. If possible, record in one session at a quality where the numbers in the UI are readable.

## How everything gets concatenated
1. **Normalize** every input to the same spec (1080p, 30 fps, H.264, no audio) with ffmpeg. This is what makes clips from different sources join cleanly. Omni clips may come out at another resolution or frame rate, so this step is needed.
2. **Assemble in Remotion**, using `timeline.json` to place each clip. This is where voice, music, captions, the diagram (F) and the end card (G) are added, and it does the actual join.
3. **Render** to `out/final.mp4`.
4. **Fallback:** if Remotion gives trouble, `ffmpeg -f concat` joins the normalized clips with the voice track laid over the top. It has no overlays, so it only produces a plain cut.

ffmpeg is the one dependency we don't have yet (`brew install ffmpeg`).

)

stream = await client.tts_stream(

        "model_name": "default",

    },
    text="This is a longer text that will be streamed."
)
